items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Georgie Smith was back again on drums... We opened at the Chikito the 1st of December... Georgie Smith said that he was not going unless he saw my contract... Bishop had more experience on drums than Georgie Smith

ctx.x: I did a couple of radio shows, one being broadcast to Sweden and a gig in Chalon-sur-Saône and left Paris the 28th of November for Bern, Switzerland.

Fred Palmer was to join me in Bern because he had finished his job in Germany. I engaged a pianist from Martinique named Pierre Jean Louis who had a style of playing that was a little like Theolionus Monk, but with more technique. Pierre was a big fellow who could drink his share of juice and some of mine, but was never drunk and always in good humour. Georgie Smith was back again on drums. A bass player named Alvin "Buddy" Banks had received his discharge from the army in Germany and had come to Paris where I…

We opened at the Chikito the 1st of December and finished the 31st of March, 1951. I had a concert in Brussels, Belgium at the Palais des Beux-Arts and played concerts with my group in Geneva, Bienne, Zurich, Neuchatel and Luzern. These dates taken place between the 2nd and 16th of April. I had a contract to play at the cinema Rex in Zurich for 11 days starting the 16th of April. I was having a longer and more successful run with this orchestra then I did with the first one. I had some arrangements that were made…
